mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) compress discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS) indicates a robust labor market, supporting corporate earnings and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when PAYEMS is above 140000.

mechanism_narrative: Strong industrial production (INDPRO > 110) indicates robust supply chain activity, supporting corporate profitability and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO > 110.

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing market activity (HOUST > 1600) indicates robust consumer spending and economic growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 1600.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate is low (FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.5%) and unemployment is high (UNRATE ≥ 6.0%), it indicates a monetary policy response to economic weakness, which typically leads to positive equity returns as the Fed eases policy to stimulate the economy over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.5% AND UNRATE ≥ 6.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When housing market activity (HOUST > 1600) and industrial production (INDPRO > 105) are both strong, it indicates a synchronized expansion in consumer and business sectors, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST > 1600 AND INDPRO > 105.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, high federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) are associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances during monetary tightening cycles when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansion (when housing market activity and retail sales are strong), the economy is overheating, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances during late-cycle expansion when HOUST > 1600 and RSAFS > 500000.
